Focus for this checkpoint: APS definition, APS pathology, APS antibodies, APS presentations, APS diagnosis, APS clinical criteria.

questions.q: Match each definition with the gestation or weight it uses — 1) Abortion 2) WHO definition of abortion 3) Intrauterine death … A) Fetal weight below 500 g, about 22 weeks B) Pregnancy loss at or after 20 weeks C) Pregnancy loss before 20 weeks
questions.exp: Abortion is pregnancy loss before 20 weeks; the WHO definition is fetal weight below 500 g, about 22 weeks; and intrauterine death is loss at or after 20 weeks. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: The WHO definition of abortion is a fetal weight below ______ g, approximately below ______ weeks.
questions.exp: The WHO definition uses a fetal weight below 500 g, approximately 22 weeks. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: Abortion is pregnancy loss before ______ weeks, whereas intrauterine death is loss at or after ______ weeks.
questions.exp: Abortion is pregnancy loss before 20 weeks of gestation, and intrauterine death is pregnancy loss at or after 20 weeks. (Book p418)

questions.q: Which statement about the period of viability is TRUE?
opts: The notes state a period of viability of 28 weeks in India
The notes state a period of viability of 24 weeks in India
The source definition puts viability at 32 weeks
Viability is reached at 20 weeks in the source notes
questions.exp: The notes state a period of viability of 28 weeks in India. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: Spontaneous abortion is subdivided into an ______ single episode or ______ abortion.
opts: Recurrent; isolated, meaning a single loss
questions.exp: In the source flowchart spontaneous abortion is subdivided into an isolated single episode and recurrent abortion with at least 3 abortions. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: An abortion that is induced medically is termed ______.
questions.exp: Induced abortion is medical termination of pregnancy. (Book p418)

questions.q: A woman who had a surgical evacuation four days ago now has fever, lower abdominal pain and an offensive vaginal discharge, and her os is open. Which feature makes this a septic abortion?
opts: The presence of septic foci in association with the abortion
Rh negativity of the mother on its own
An open internal os by itself, without any infection
Fetal cardiac activity still seen on the scan
questions.exp: Any abortion with septic foci is a septic abortion; neither Rh negativity, an open os alone nor fetal cardiac activity defines it. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: In India, abortion is defined as termination of pregnancy before ______ weeks of gestation or the birth of a fetus weighing less than ______ g.
questions.exp: Indian law uses the 28-week or 1000 g definition of viability, so expulsion before that limit and weight is called abortion. (Book p418)

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman has a single isolated first-trimester pregnancy loss. She has no history of thrombosis, no cervical surgery and no systemic disease. What is the most common cause of this kind of loss?
questions.exp: Chromosomal anomaly is the most common cause of an isolated first- or second-trimester abortion, and aneuploidy is the most common category. (Book p418)

questions.q: Which statement about chromosomal anomalies in isolated abortion is TRUE?
opts: Aneuploidy is the most common category
Balanced translocation is the most common category
Triploidy accounts for most isolated abortions
Mitochondrial mutations are the leading category
questions.exp: Aneuploidy is listed as the most common chromosomal anomaly in isolated abortion. (Book p418)

questions.q: All of the following are listed chromosomal abnormalities in isolated abortion EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The source order is aneuploidy, then trisomy, then monosomy (Turner syndrome), then trisomy 16; a mitochondrial mutation is not listed. (Book p418)

questions.q: All of the following are listed causes or risk factors for isolated abortion EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Listed risk factors are a previous abortion and increasing maternal age, with chromosomal anomaly the commonest cause; daily walking is not a risk factor. (Book p418)

questions.q: Which statement about maternal age and isolated abortion is TRUE?
opts: The risk of isolated abortion increases with maternal age
Maternal age has no effect on the risk of isolated abortion
Only paternal age affects the risk of isolated abortion
The risk falls to zero after the age of 35 years
questions.exp: Increasing maternal age is a listed risk factor for isolated abortion. (Book p418)

questions.q: Which statement about infection and recurrent abortion is TRUE?
opts: Infections do not cause recurrent abortion
All infections are the commonest cause of recurrent abortion
TORCH serology always proves a diagnosis of recurrent abortion
VDRL testing is mandatory in every case of recurrent loss
questions.exp: The notes state that infections do not cause recurrent abortion. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: In congenital syphilis the pregnancy prognosis follows ______ law, improving as the number of pregnancies ______.
questions.exp: Kassowitz law states that the pregnancy prognosis is proportional to the number of pregnancies in syphilis; stillbirth is more common than abortion. (Book p418)

questions.q: All of the following infections are associated with spontaneous abortion EXCEPT:
opts: Human papillomavirus infection of the cervix
questions.exp: Cervical HPV causes warts and neoplasia, not pregnancy loss; listeria, syphilis, CMV, rubella, toxoplasma and parvovirus all cause loss. (Book p418)

questions.q: Fill up: The most lethal trisomy is trisomy ______, while the most viable is trisomy ______.
questions.exp: Trisomy 16 is the most lethal in the note, and trisomy 21 is the most viable, with abortion its most common outcome. (Book p419)

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman has a second-trimester loss and products of conception are sent for karyotyping, which returns trisomy 21. How is this trisomy described in the notes?
opts: The most viable, with abortion as its commonest outcome
The most lethal of all the autosomal trisomies
Incompatible with implantation, so never seen in losses
Always inherited from a parental balanced translocation
questions.exp: Trisomy 21 is the most viable trisomy and abortion is its most common outcome; trisomy 16 is the most lethal. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which statement about HIV and pregnancy loss is TRUE?
opts: HIV is neither abortogenic nor teratogenic
HIV is abortogenic but not teratogenic
HIV is teratogenic but not abortogenic
HIV is always both abortogenic and teratogenic
questions.exp: The source explicitly states that HIV is neither abortogenic nor teratogenic. (Book p419)

questions.q: Fill up: Recurrent abortion is defined as at least ______ consecutive pregnancy losses before ______ weeks.
questions.exp: Recurrent abortion is at least 3 consecutive pregnancy losses before 20 weeks. (Book p419)

questions.q: What ASRM definition of recurrent pregnancy loss is stated?
questions.exp: ASRM defines recurrent loss as at least 2 confirmed pregnancy losses. (Book p419)

questions.q: How can pregnancy loss be confirmed for the ASRM recurrent-loss definition?
questions.exp: Confirmation is by histopathological examination or USG. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common group of causes of recurrent abortion?
questions.exp: Endocrine causes are the most common group, ahead of uterine causes. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common individual cause of recurrent abortion?
questions.exp: APLA syndrome is the most common individual cause. (Book p419)

questions.q: Fill up: The commonest cause of a sporadic first-trimester abortion is a ______, and the single commonest chromosomal abnormality found is ______.
questions.exp: About half of early losses are chromosomally abnormal, with autosomal trisomy the commonest abnormality, followed by monosomy X and polyploidy. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common endocrine cause of recurrent abortion?
questions.exp: Hypothyroidism is the most common endocrine cause. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which endocrine conditions are listed among recurrent-abortion causes?
opts: Uncontrolled diabetes, PCOS, and raised prolactin
questions.exp: Uncontrolled diabetes, PCOS, and increased prolactin are listed endocrine causes. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common uterine cause of recurrent first-trimester abortion?
questions.exp: Septate uterus is the most common uterine cause of first-trimester abortion. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which congenital uterine anomaly is next in frequency after septate uterus in the source list?
questions.exp: The source ranks septate uterus above bicornuate uterus. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which acquired uterine causes are listed for recurrent abortion?
opts: Cervical incompetence, a submucous fibroid and Asherman syndrome
Placenta previa, which implants low and bleeds repeatedly
A previous ectopic pregnancy, which scars the uterine cavity
An ovarian cyst, which distorts the outline of the uterus
questions.exp: Acquired uterine causes of recurrent loss are cervical weakness, cavity-distorting fibroids and intrauterine adhesions. (Book p419)

questions.q: What proportion of recurrent abortions can be due to chromosomal abnormalities?
questions.exp: Chromosomal abnormalities may account for 2–5% of recurrent abortions. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is the most common chromosomal abnormality in recurrent abortion?
opts: Trisomy 16 with a full autosomal trisomy
questions.exp: The most common chromosomal abnormality in recurrent abortion is a balanced chromosomal translocation. (Book p419)

questions.q: Match the endocrine cause with its association — 1) Poorly controlled diabetes 2) Luteal phase deficiency 3) Thyroid autoimmunity … A) Loss is linked to thyroid antibodies even when thyroid function tests are normal B) Losses occur mainly in the first trimester, so control before conception matters most C) Progesterone support helps only in selected women with recurrent loss
questions.exp: Diabetic loss tracks glycaemic control at conception, thyroid antibodies mark risk independent of function, and progesterone has a narrow role. (Book p419)

questions.q: When should recurrent-abortion investigations begin according to the notes?
questions.exp: The source says investigations should begin after two abortions. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which targeted investigation is used when an endocrine cause of recurrent abortion is suspected?
questions.exp: TSH is performed if an endocrine cause is suspected. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which targeted investigation is used when a uterine cause of recurrent abortion is suspected?
questions.exp: TVS is performed if a uterine cause is suspected. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which two etiologic tests are routinely included after recurrent losses in the source plan?
opts: Serum bile acids and HbA1c estimation
APLA antibody testing and parental karyotyping
questions.exp: After recurrent losses the source plan routinely includes the etiologic tests APLA antibody testing and parental karyotyping. (Book p419)

questions.q: Which test is specifically not done for recurrent abortion in the source notes?
opts: TVS when uterine cause is suspected
questions.exp: TORCH testing, VDRL, and thrombophilia testing are listed as not done. (Book p419)

questions.q: All of the following are part of the standard evaluation of recurrent pregnancy loss EXCEPT:
opts: Partner karyotyping after a single first-trimester loss
Lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibody testing
Thyroid function, prolactin and glycaemic assessment
Three-dimensional ultrasound or hysteroscopy for a uterine anomaly
questions.exp: Investigation begins after three consecutive losses (or earlier if indicated); a single sporadic loss needs no work-up. (Book p419)

questions.q: What is cervical incompetence by definition?
opts: Painful first-trimester abortion from uterine contractions
Any open external os at delivery
Spontaneous dilatation of an incompetent internal os causing painless second-trimester abortion
questions.exp: Cervical incompetence is spontaneous internal-os dilatation causing painless second-trimester loss. (Book p420)

questions.q: What history supports cervical incompetence?
questions.exp: A history of recurrent (at least 3) painless second-trimester abortions supports cervical incompetence. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which nonpregnant test can support cervical incompetence by showing passage without resistance?
questions.exp: In nonpregnant women, passage of Hegar dilator no. 8 without resistance is a diagnostic clue. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which Foley catheter finding supports cervical incompetence in a nonpregnant woman?
opts: No. 16 Foley with a 1-mL inflated bulb passes without resistance
No. 8 Foley with 10 mL inflated bulb cannot pass
questions.exp: Passage of no. 16 Foley with bulb filled with 1 mL water without resistance supports the diagnosis. (Book p420)

questions.q: What is the investigation of choice for cervical incompetence during pregnancy?
questions.exp: TVS is the investigation of choice in pregnancy. (Book p420)

questions.q: What cervical length is normal in pregnancy according to the source table?
questions.exp: The normal pregnancy cervical length is 4–5 cm. (Book p420)

questions.q: What TVS cervical-length value supports cervical incompetence?
questions.exp: Cervical length ≤2.5 cm supports cervical incompetence. (Book p420)

questions.q: Fill up: A cervical length below ______ mm before 24 weeks is taken as evidence of cervical weakness, and the measurement must be made by ______ sonography.
questions.exp: Transvaginal measurement is the standard; an empty bladder, a full-thickness view and a short closed cervix below 25 mm mark risk. (Book p420)

questions.q: What is the normal cervical shape on TVS in pregnancy?
questions.exp: A normal cervical shape is T shaped. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which funneling progression is characteristic of cervical incompetence?
questions.exp: Cervical incompetence shows Y→V→U funneling. (Book p420)

questions.q: Why is cervical length inversely related to cervical dilatation?
opts: The internal os closes the cervix
questions.exp: As the cervix dilates, it is taken up, so length falls. (Book p420)

questions.q: What is the principle of cervical cerclage?
opts: Place sutures around the internal os
questions.exp: Cerclage places sutures around the internal os. (Book p420)

questions.q: What is the history-based indication for cervical cerclage?
opts: A normal cervix on transvaginal scan with no history of any pregnancy loss
Maternal age above forty alone, even with no previous pregnancy loss
At least two painless second-trimester losses, irrespective of the scan findings
Any single first-trimester loss, since one loss reliably predicts another
questions.exp: A history-based indication is recurrent painless mid-trimester loss, typically two or more, and it applies whatever the cervical length shows. (Book p420)

questions.q: What ultrasound-based history indication for cerclage is listed after one painless second-trimester loss?
questions.exp: One painless T2 abortion plus cervical length <2.5 cm is ultrasound-based indication. (Book p420)

questions.q: What history plus TVS finding supports cerclage after early preterm labor?
opts: Early PTL history with cervical length less than 2.5 cm
Early PTL with cervical length over 5 cm
Only a positive urine pregnancy test
questions.exp: Early PTL plus cervical length <2.5 cm is an indication. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about cervical incompetence is TRUE?
opts: It is essentially a clinical diagnosis of painless second-trimester dilatation with recurrent mid-trimester losses
A cervical length above 30 mm on transvaginal scan confirms the diagnosis
It classically presents with painful contractions and heavy bleeding in the first trimester
It is diagnosed by measuring serum progesterone in the middle of the second trimester
questions.exp: Painless dilation with recurrent second-trimester loss is the hallmark; ultrasound supports the diagnosis but does not define it. (Book p420)

questions.q: What physical finding is the basis for emergency cervical cerclage?
opts: Ultrasound evidence of fetal macrosomia before term
A pregnant woman under 24 weeks with a dilated cervix
A closed cervix at 39 weeks with a normal lie
Only a positive indirect Coombs test result
questions.exp: Emergency cervical cerclage is based on a pregnant woman under 24 weeks with a dilated cervix. (Book p420)

questions.q: What is the earliest gestational age at which cervical cerclage is done according to the notes?
questions.exp: The earliest cerclage is done at 12 weeks. (Book p420)

questions.q: Why is progesterone given in the cervical-incompetence protocol?
questions.exp: Progesterone is used to prevent preterm labor. (Book p420)

questions.q: What progesterone schedule is stated for preterm-labor prevention?
opts: Start at 12–24 weeks and stop at 36 weeks
Start at 36 weeks and stop at delivery
questions.exp: Progesterone is started between 12–24 weeks and stopped at 36 weeks. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which history is an indication for progesterone in the source plan?
opts: Only a previous molar pregnancy, to prevent trophoblastic disease
A history of painless second-trimester abortion or of preterm labour
Only a previous normal term delivery, to shorten the latent phase
Only an Rh-negative pregnancy, to prevent maternal sensitisation
questions.exp: In the source plan progesterone is used in a woman with a history of painless second-trimester abortion or preterm labour. (Book p420)

questions.q: Which ultrasound/care finding is an indication for progesterone?
opts: Cervical length less than 2.5 cm or after a cerclage
Cervical length of 5 cm with no history
questions.exp: Progesterone is indicated for short cervix <2.5 cm and if cerclage has been done. (Book p420)

questions.q: What treatment is given for a history of at least 2 painless second-trimester abortions?
opts: Progesterone from 12 weeks plus cervical cerclage
questions.exp: At least two painless T2 losses receive progesterone from 12 weeks plus cerclage. (Book p421)

questions.q: For one painless second-trimester loss or early preterm labor, when is the cervical ultrasound reassessment performed?
questions.exp: The algorithm performs ultrasound at 14 weeks. (Book p421)

questions.q: After one prior painless T2 loss/early PTL, what is used if cervical length at 14 weeks is below 2.5 cm?
opts: No treatment is given at all
questions.exp: After one prior painless second-trimester loss or early preterm labour, a cervical length under 2.5 cm at 14 weeks is managed with cerclage plus progesterone. (Book p421)

questions.q: After one prior painless T2 loss/early PTL, what is used if cervical length at 14 weeks is at least 2.5 cm?
questions.exp: If cervical length is ≥2.5 cm, give progesterone only. (Book p421)

questions.q: A 28-year-old at 20 weeks with two previous mid-trimester losses has membranes bulging through a cervix dilated to 3 cm. She has no contractions, no bleeding and no fever. What is the management?
opts: Rescue or emergency cerclage after excluding infection, with antibiotics, tocolysis and corticosteroids
Immediate induction of labour, because exposed membranes cannot be saved
Discharge with bed rest and no intervention, since the cervix is already dilated
Vaginal progesterone alone, because no suture can be placed once membranes bulge
questions.exp: Rescue cerclage is worthwhile in selected women once infection is excluded and membranes are reduced, though benefit is smaller than with elective cerclage. (Book p421)

questions.q: What management is used for short cervix under 2.5 cm with no history of abortion?
questions.exp: Short cervical length without loss history is managed with progesterone. (Book p421)

questions.q: What are prerequisites for rescue/emergency cerclage?
opts: Cervix fully dilated with ruptured membranes
Cervix less than 4 cm dilated, intact membranes, and no infection
questions.exp: Rescue cerclage requires <4 cm dilatation, intact/bulging membranes acceptable, and no infection. (Book p421)

questions.q: What is the most common cerclage approach?
questions.exp: Transvaginal cerclage is the most common approach. (Book p421)

questions.q: When are sutures removed after transvaginal cerclage?
questions.exp: Transvaginal sutures are removed at 37 weeks, allowing vaginal delivery. (Book p421)

questions.q: What delivery consequence follows transabdominal cerclage?
opts: Suture is left in place and delivery is by LSCS
Suture is removed at 37 weeks for vaginal delivery
questions.exp: Transabdominal cerclage leaves suture in place and delivery is by LSCS. (Book p421)

questions.q: When is transabdominal cerclage used?
questions.exp: Transabdominal cerclage is done if transvaginal cerclage fails. (Book p421)

questions.q: All of the following are true of transabdominal cervico-isthmic cerclage EXCEPT:
opts: It is placed vaginally and the suture is removed at 37 weeks
It is chosen when the cervix is very short, scarred or a vaginal cerclage has failed
Delivery must be by caesarean section, since the suture cannot be removed
It is usually placed before pregnancy or in early pregnancy, often laparoscopically
questions.exp: Transabdominal cerclage is placed at the cervico-isthmic junction from above and commits the woman to caesarean delivery. (Book p421)

questions.q: What type of suture is used in McDonald cerclage?
opts: Continuous suture close to internal os after bladder dissection
Purse string in the portio vaginalis
questions.exp: McDonald uses a purse-string suture in portio vaginalis. (Book p422)

questions.q: Is bladder dissection performed in McDonald cerclage?
questions.exp: Bladder dissection is not done in McDonald cerclage. (Book p422)

questions.q: What suture material is listed for McDonald cerclage?
questions.exp: McDonald cerclage uses nonabsorbable polypropylene. (Book p422)

questions.q: Which feature characterizes Shirodkar cerclage?
opts: Continuous suture placed close to internal os after bladder dissection
Purse-string in portio without bladder dissection
questions.exp: Shirodkar uses a continuous suture close to internal os and includes bladder dissection. (Book p422)

questions.q: How does Shirodkar success compare with McDonald cerclage in the source table?
opts: McDonald has a higher success rate
They are exactly identical by definition
Shirodkar has a higher success rate
questions.exp: The table lists higher success for Shirodkar and lower for McDonald. (Book p422)

questions.q: What suture material is listed for Shirodkar cerclage?
questions.exp: Shirodkar cerclage uses Mersilene tape. (Book p422)

questions.q: When is Wurm cerclage used?
opts: Emergency cerclage when the cervix is dilated
questions.exp: Wurm is the emergency cerclage used when the cervix is dilated. (Book p422)

questions.q: How are the sutures placed in Wurm cerclage?
opts: One suture around the uterine fundus
Two sutures, one anteroposterior and one transverse
questions.exp: Wurm uses two sutures: in AP and transverse directions. (Book p422)

questions.q: Match the cerclage with its technique — 1) McDonald 2) Shirodkar 3) Transabdominal … A) A purse-string suture at the cervicovaginal junction placed without any dissection B) A submucosal tape at the level of the internal os placed after reflecting the bladder C) A suture placed at the cervico-isthmic junction from above, usually by laparoscopy
questions.exp: McDonald is the simple purse-string, Shirodkar needs bladder reflection to reach the internal os, and the abdominal route is reserved for failed or impossible vaginal cerclage. (Book p422)

questions.q: What gestational window is given for cerclage suture application?
opts: 14–24 weeks; RCOG allows up to 28 weeks
questions.exp: Application is 14–24 weeks, with RCOG guidance up to 28 weeks. (Book p422)

questions.q: Why may a vaginal cerclage be removed earlier than 37 weeks?
opts: Preterm labour or premature rupture of the membranes
Normal fetal movements with a reassuring cardiotocograph
Mild nausea in the second trimester of the pregnancy
Rh negativity of the mother with no evidence of sensitisation
questions.exp: A vaginal cerclage may be removed earlier than 37 weeks if preterm labour or premature rupture of membranes supervenes. (Book p422)

questions.q: What mode of delivery follows vaginal cerclage after its normal removal?
questions.exp: After vaginal cerclage removal at 37 weeks, mode of delivery is vaginal. (Book p422)

questions.q: What is the indication for abdominal cerclage?
opts: First painless loss with normal cervix
questions.exp: Abdominal cerclage is indicated if vaginal cerclage fails. (Book p422)

questions.q: Which technique for abdominal cerclage can be done in both pregnant and nonpregnant women?
questions.exp: Laparoscopic abdominal cerclage can be done in pregnant and nonpregnant women. (Book p422)

questions.q: Which obsolete abdominal cerclage technique is done in nonpregnant women and requires avoiding pregnancy for 3 months after surgery?
questions.exp: LASH/LASH surgery is obsolete, removes part of cervix before suture, and requires 3-month pregnancy avoidance. (Book p422)

questions.q: Fill up: Elective cerclage is typically performed at ______ weeks of gestation, and the suture is removed at ______ weeks.
questions.exp: Elective cerclage is placed once viability and anatomy are confirmed around 12-14 weeks and removed near term before labour begins. (Book p422)

questions.q: When is a tocolytic indicated with cerclage in the source notes?
opts: Cervical length under 25 mm on ultrasound, with emergency cerclage
Every history-based or elective cerclage as routine practice
Any normal pregnancy, given routinely as a prophylactic measure
Only after delivery, to treat postpartum uterine atony
questions.exp: In the source notes a tocolytic is used with cerclage only when the ultrasound cervical length is below 25 mm and the cerclage is an emergency one. (Book p423)

questions.q: When are antibiotics used with cervical cerclage?
questions.exp: Antibiotics are used in emergency cerclage with bulging membranes, not currently recommended in other cases. (Book p423)

questions.q: Which clinical status is a contraindication to cervical cerclage?
opts: Short cervix with a painless-loss history
questions.exp: Uterine contractions/preterm labor are a cerclage contraindication. (Book p423)

questions.q: Which fetal conditions are contraindications to cervical cerclage?
questions.exp: Fetal distress and fetal anomaly are contraindications. (Book p423)

questions.q: Which maternal/obstetric conditions are contraindications to cervical cerclage?
opts: Ruptured membranes, bleeding per vaginum, or current pelvic infection
Mild nausea, normal discharge, and Rh negativity
questions.exp: Ruptured membranes, P/V bleeding, and current pelvic infection are contraindications. (Book p423)

questions.q: What is the relative contraindication to cervical cerclage?
questions.exp: Placenta previa is the relative contraindication. (Book p423)

questions.q: All of the following contraindicate cervical cerclage EXCEPT:
opts: A previous uncomplicated term delivery with no history of pregnancy loss
Active vaginal bleeding or ruptured membranes
Chorioamnionitis or evidence of intrauterine infection
Lethal fetal anomaly or intrauterine fetal death
questions.exp: Cerclage is contraindicated by bleeding, rupture, infection and fetal death; a woman with no history suggesting weakness simply does not need one. (Book p423)

questions.q: What is another name for antiphospholipid antibody syndrome?
questions.exp: APLA syndrome is also called antiphospholipid syndrome. (Book p424)

questions.q: What is the key pathologic effect of acquired antiphospholipid antibodies?
questions.exp: Acquired antibodies against phospholipids cause thrombosis. (Book p424)

questions.q: Which antibody is included among APS antibodies?
questions.exp: Lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, and anti-beta2 glycoprotein are listed APS antibodies. (Book p424)

questions.q: Which arterial events are listed presentations of APS?
questions.exp: APS can present as arterial thrombosis, including cerebral or myocardial infarction. (Book p424)

questions.q: What placental complication underlies abortion, IUGR, and preterm labor in APS?
opts: Maternal TSH crossing the placenta and damaging the cytotrophoblast
Placental thrombosis and infarction causing uteroplacental insufficiency
Placental overperfusion from failure of physiological conversion
Fetal hyperinsulinaemia from transplacental maternal antibody transfer
questions.exp: Placental thrombosis in APS causes abortion, uteroplacental insufficiency with IUGR, and preterm labour. (Book p424)

questions.q: What combination is required to diagnose APS using modified Sapporo/Sydney criteria?
opts: At least one clinical criterion and one laboratory criterion
questions.exp: APS diagnosis requires one clinical plus one laboratory criterion. (Book p424)

questions.q: Which thrombotic history fulfills a clinical APS criterion?
questions.exp: History of arterial or venous thrombosis is a clinical APS criterion. (Book p424)

questions.q: What recurrent early-loss history fulfills a clinical APS criterion?
opts: At least 3 first-trimester abortions before 10 weeks
questions.exp: A history of at least 3 first-trimester abortions before 10 weeks is a clinical criterion. (Book p424)

questions.q: What later fetal-loss history fulfills a clinical APS criterion?
opts: At least one fetal loss after 10 weeks
questions.exp: One or more fetal losses beyond 10 weeks is a clinical APS criterion. (Book p424)

questions.q: What preterm-delivery history fulfills a clinical APS criterion?
opts: Labor due to PROM without complications only
At least one preterm labor before 32 weeks due to UPI or PIH
questions.exp: A preterm birth before 32 weeks associated with UPI/PIH is a clinical criterion. (Book p424)

questions.q: Fill up: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome is diagnosed when a clinical criterion is combined with persistently positive ______, ______ or ______.
opts: lupus anticoagulant; anticardiolipin antibody; anti-beta2 glycoprotein I antibody
rheumatoid factor; antinuclear antibody; anti-CCP antibody
questions.exp: The three criteria antibodies are lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin and anti-beta2 glycoprotein I, each needing confirmation 12 weeks later. (Book p424)

questions.q: How must anticardiolipin antibody positivity be documented for APS diagnosis?
opts: One positive result on one day only
IgG or IgM positive on two occasions 12 weeks apart
questions.exp: Anticardiolipin IgG/IgM must be positive on two tests 12 weeks apart. (Book p424)

questions.q: How must anti-beta2-glycoprotein antibody positivity be documented for APS diagnosis?
opts: IgG or IgM positive on two occasions 12 weeks apart
questions.exp: Anti-beta2-glycoprotein IgG/IgM needs two positives 12 weeks apart. (Book p424)

questions.q: Why can lupus anticoagulant not be directly detected by ELISA?
opts: It has anticoagulant effect in vitro but is thrombotic in vivo
It is produced only after delivery
questions.exp: Lupus anticoagulant cannot be directly detected by ELISA; it is anticoagulant in vitro but thrombotic in vivo. (Book p424)

questions.q: Which laboratory pattern helps indirectly detect lupus anticoagulant?
opts: A prolonged dilute Russell viper venom time, kaolin clotting time and isolated raised aPTT
A raised glycated haemoglobin, which reflects the thrombotic tendency of the disease
A high serum bile acid concentration, which prolongs the phospholipid clotting tests
A shortened activated partial thromboplastin time with a normal prothrombin time
questions.exp: Lupus anticoagulant is detected functionally: a prolonged phospholipid-dependent clotting time that does not correct on mixing. (Book p424)

questions.q: Match the antiphospholipid test with how it is performed — 1) Lupus anticoagulant 2) Anticardiolipin antibody 3) Anti-beta2 glycoprotein I … A) A phospholipid-dependent clotting test such as the dilute Russell viper venom time B) IgG or IgM measured by ELISA, medium or high titre, above the 99th centile C) IgG or IgM measured by ELISA, above the 99th centile, confirmed 12 weeks later
questions.exp: Lupus anticoagulant is a functional clotting assay, while anticardiolipin and anti-beta2 glycoprotein I are ELISA-based and all need repeat confirmation. (Book p424)

questions.q: What treatment is recommended in APS with a history of thrombosis or abortion?
questions.exp: APS with thrombosis or abortion history is managed with heparin plus aspirin. (Book p425)

questions.q: What treatment is recommended in APS with a history of preterm labor due to uteroplacental insufficiency?
questions.exp: APS with prior PTL due to UPI receives aspirin alone in the source plan. (Book p425)

questions.q: When is aspirin started in pregnancy for APS according to the notes?
opts: As soon as the pregnancy is diagnosed by a positive urine pregnancy test
After delivery, once the placenta has been examined
Only from 36 completed weeks of gestation onwards
Before menarche, since the antibody persists for life
questions.exp: Low-dose aspirin is started as soon as pregnancy is confirmed in women with antiphospholipid syndrome. (Book p425)

questions.q: When is heparin started for APS in pregnancy?
questions.exp: Heparin begins once intrauterine pregnancy is confirmed. (Book p425)

questions.q: When are anticoagulants stopped in APS labor management?
questions.exp: Anticoagulants are stopped intrapartum. (Book p425)

questions.q: When are anticoagulants resumed/continued after vaginal delivery in APS?
questions.exp: Anticoagulation is continued postpartum beginning 6 hours after vaginal delivery. (Book p425)

questions.q: When are anticoagulants resumed/continued after LSCS in APS?
questions.exp: Anticoagulation is continued 12 hours after LSCS. (Book p425)

questions.q: What is the drug of choice for a nonpregnant woman with APS and history of thrombosis?
opts: Heparin plus aspirin indefinitely in every case
questions.exp: Warfarin is the drug of choice for nonpregnant APS with thrombosis history. (Book p425)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about antiphospholipid syndrome in pregnancy is TRUE?
opts: Thrombotic risk is highest in the puerperium, so thromboprophylaxis is continued for six weeks after delivery
Risk returns to normal the moment the placenta is delivered, so prophylaxis can stop at delivery
Low-molecular-weight heparin must be replaced by warfarin throughout the first trimester
Low-dose aspirin and heparin are contraindicated in pregnancy because of the risk of fetal bleeding
questions.exp: Heparin does not cross the placenta and with low-dose aspirin is the standard treatment; postpartum thromboprophylaxis is essential. (Book p425)

questions.q: What defines threatened abortion?
opts: The internal os is open with no chance of continuation
The abortion process has started but no products of conception have been expelled, and it is reversible
All products of conception have been expelled
questions.exp: Threatened abortion is a reversible process with no POC expelled. (Book p425)

questions.q: What clinical and cervical findings are typical of threatened abortion?
opts: Heavy bleeding with an open os and expelled POC
No bleeding with an open os
Spotting P/V with or without pain and a closed internal os
questions.exp: Threatened abortion has spotting, possible pain, and a closed os. (Book p425)

questions.q: What ultrasound finding supports threatened abortion?
questions.exp: Cardiac activity is present in threatened abortion. (Book p425)

questions.q: What management is listed for threatened abortion?
opts: Immediate suction evacuation in all cases
questions.exp: Threatened abortion is managed with reassurance and advice to avoid intercourse. (Book p425)

questions.q: What is the stated role of progesterone and hCG in threatened abortion?
opts: Both are contraindicated because of sepsis
Progesterone benefit is ill-defined; hCG has no benefit
questions.exp: The notes call progesterone benefit ill-defined and state hCG has no benefit. (Book p425)

questions.q: What defines inevitable abortion?
opts: POC is completely expelled and symptoms have resolved
A closed os with fetal cardiac activity
The abortion process has started with no POC expelled and is irreversible
questions.exp: Inevitable abortion is irreversible though POC has not yet been expelled. (Book p425)

questions.q: What clinical/cervical findings distinguish inevitable abortion?
opts: Bleeding and abdominal pain with an open internal os
Purulent discharge with empty uterus only
questions.exp: Inevitable abortion has bleeding, abdominal pain, and an open os. (Book p425)

questions.q: What ultrasound and management combination fits inevitable abortion?
opts: Absent cardiac activity; expedite by medical abortion or suction evacuation
questions.exp: Inevitable abortion shows absent cardiac activity and is expedited medically or by suction evacuation. (Book p425)

questions.q: A 26-year-old at 9 weeks has light vaginal bleeding and a closed cervical os. Ultrasound shows a live embryo with a small subchorionic haematoma. What is the appropriate management?
opts: Reassurance and avoidance of strenuous activity, since no drug or bed rest has been shown to change the outcome in most cases
Immediate evacuation of the uterus to prevent heavy haemorrhage
Urgent cervical cerclage, since first-trimester bleeding indicates cervical incompetence
High-dose intramuscular progesterone continued throughout the pregnancy
questions.exp: Most threatened abortions continue; intervention is reserved for inevitable, incomplete or missed abortion and for heavy bleeding. (Book p425)

questions.q: What defines incomplete abortion?
opts: A viable fetal heart with closed os
Abortion has begun and products of conception are incompletely expelled
All products are expelled with no current bleeding
questions.exp: Incomplete abortion means POC have been incompletely expelled. (Book p425)

questions.q: Which constellation is typical of incomplete abortion?
opts: No symptoms, a closed os and an empty uterus
Only spotting, with fetal cardiac activity still present
A painless second-trimester loss with no cervical dilatation
Bleeding and pain with expelled POC, an open os, and POC coming out
questions.exp: Incomplete abortion typically presents with bleeding and abdominal pain, a history of expelled products of conception, an open os and POC coming out. (Book p425)

questions.q: What ultrasound and management approach fits incomplete abortion?
opts: Incomplete POC; maintain vitals if shock and expedite abortion
questions.exp: USG shows incomplete POC; stabilize shock if present and expedite abortion. (Book p425)

questions.q: What defines complete abortion?
opts: Sepsis is always present in these cases by definition
The entire abortion completes spontaneously after all POC are expelled
No products of conception have been expelled at all
The os is open with products of conception retained
questions.exp: Complete abortion is defined as the entire abortion completing spontaneously once all products of conception have been expelled. (Book p425)

questions.q: Which clinical/USG pattern supports complete abortion?
opts: No history of POC expulsion and retained tissue
Past bleeding and POC expulsion with no current bleeding, closed os, and empty uterus
Current severe bleeding with open os
questions.exp: Complete abortion features past bleeding/POC expulsion, no current bleeding, closed os, and empty uterus. (Book p425)

questions.q: What management is listed after complete abortion?
opts: Immediate cervical cerclage before the woman leaves
Immediate laparotomy to exclude an ectopic gestation
No Rh-related consideration is needed at all after this event
Reassurance and anti-D if Rh-positive exposure requires it
questions.exp: After complete abortion the listed management is reassurance and anti-D if Rh-positive exposure requires it. (Book p425)

questions.q: How is missed abortion primarily diagnosed?
questions.exp: Missed abortion is ultrasound based. (Book p426)

questions.q: What symptom profile is typical of missed abortion?
opts: Usually no symptoms, possibly brown discharge
Heavy fever and purulent discharge in every case
questions.exp: Missed abortion often has no symptoms but may have brown discharge. (Book p426)

questions.q: How does uterine size compare with period of gestation in missed abortion?
opts: Equal to or less than POG
questions.exp: The table shows uterine height equal to or less than period of gestation. (Book p426)

questions.q: What is the internal-os finding in missed abortion?
questions.exp: The internal os is closed in missed abortion. (Book p426)

questions.q: Match the type of abortion with its findings — 1) Threatened 2) Inevitable 3) Incomplete … A) Bleeding and pain with a dilated os and membranes that may rupture B) Partial expulsion of products with an open os and heavy bleeding C) Bleeding with a closed os and a live fetus, so the pregnancy may continue
questions.exp: Threatened abortion has a closed os and a live fetus, inevitable abortion has a dilated os, and incomplete abortion has retained products. (Book p426)

questions.q: Which mean-sac-diameter finding confirms missed abortion?
opts: MSD at least 25 mm with no fetal pole
questions.exp: MSD ≥25 mm without fetal pole is a diagnostic ultrasound criterion. (Book p426)

questions.q: Which CRL finding confirms missed abortion?
opts: CRL at least 7 mm with absent cardiac activity
CRL 2 mm with present cardiac activity
CRL below 5 mm with normal heart
questions.exp: CRL ≥7 mm with absent cardiac activity is diagnostic. (Book p426)

questions.q: What serial cardiac finding can diagnose missed abortion?
opts: Cardiac activity previously present but now absent
questions.exp: Previously documented cardiac activity that is absent now supports missed abortion. (Book p426)

questions.q: What management options are listed for missed abortion?
opts: Cervical cerclage with bed rest until term
Middle cerebral artery Doppler surveillance only
Medical abortion or suction evacuation of the uterus
Reassurance and expectant management without intervention
questions.exp: Missed abortion can be managed with medical abortion or suction evacuation. (Book p426)

questions.q: In a woman with abortion and shock features, what is the most common cause listed?
opts: Septic abortion, followed by incomplete abortion
questions.exp: Septic abortion is the most common cause of shock in abortion, followed by incomplete abortion. (Book p426)

questions.q: What association should be considered with abortion history and raised aPTT?
questions.exp: Abortion history plus raised aPTT suggests APLA syndrome. (Book p426)

questions.q: What defines septic abortion?
questions.exp: Septic abortion is septic foci in any abortion. (Book p426)

questions.q: Which symptoms are characteristic of septic abortion?
opts: Painless bleeding alone, with no systemic upset whatsoever
No systemic symptoms ever, because the infection stays localised
Fever and chills, abdominal pain, vomiting and a purulent vaginal discharge
Palmar pruritus, which is the only symptom that reliably appears
questions.exp: Septic abortion is a spreading infection: fever and chills, abdominal pain, gastrointestinal upset and purulent discharge. (Book p426)

questions.q: What severe presentation may occur in septic abortion?
questions.exp: Septic abortion may present as shock/toxic shock syndrome. (Book p426)

questions.q: Fill up: Missed abortion is diagnosed when the mean sac diameter is above ______ mm with no embryo, or the crown-rump length is above ______ mm with no heartbeat.
questions.exp: These thresholds prevent the tragic error of diagnosing pregnancy loss from a scan that is simply too early to show the embryo. (Book p426)

questions.q: What is grade 1 septic abortion?
questions.exp: Grade 1 infection is limited to the uterus. (Book p426)

questions.q: What is grade 2 septic abortion?
questions.exp: Grade 2 infection spreads to pelvic organs. (Book p426)

questions.q: What is grade 3 septic abortion?
questions.exp: Grade 3 septic abortion includes peritonitis, shock, or renal failure. (Book p426)

questions.q: What antibiotic regimen is listed for septic abortion?
questions.exp: The recommended regimen is ampicillin, gentamicin, and metronidazole. (Book p426)

questions.q: Which organism is specifically noted never to cause toxic shock syndrome?
questions.exp: The source note says TSS is never caused by E. coli. (Book p426)

questions.q: All of the following describe grade III septic abortion EXCEPT:
opts: Infection confined to the uterine cavity with no systemic signs
Peritonitis with infection spreading beyond the pelvis
Septic shock with hypotension and oliguria
Endotoxic shock with renal cortical necrosis or disseminated intravascular coagulation
questions.exp: Grade I infection is confined to the uterus, grade II spreads to the pelvis and parametrium, and grade III means peritonitis, shock or organ failure. (Book p426)

questions.q: Under the stated MTP Act 2021 amendment, up to what gestation is MTP allowed for congenital anomalies?
opts: No upper limit in every case
questions.exp: The stated amendment permits MTP for congenital anomalies up to 24 weeks. (Book p427)

questions.q: Under the stated MTP Act 2021 amendment, up to what gestation is MTP allowed for contraceptive failure?
questions.exp: MTP for contraceptive failure is listed up to 20 weeks. (Book p427)

questions.q: What is required for MTP in severe congenital anomalies with no upper gestational limit?
opts: One doctor only regardless of age
questions.exp: Severe congenital anomalies have no upper limit but need medical-board approval. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which specialty is part of the listed medical-board composition for MTP?
questions.exp: The board includes a gynecologist, radiologist, pediatrician, and person assigned by the state. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which nonclinical member is listed as part of the MTP medical board?
opts: A person assigned by the state
questions.exp: The medical board includes a person assigned by the state. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which circumstance is a listed indication for MTP?
questions.exp: Rape is a listed MTP indication. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which health-based indication is listed for MTP?
opts: To treat asymptomatic bacteriuria found in the pregnant woman
To prevent the onset of normal spontaneous labour at term
To save the woman's life or prevent grave physical or mental injury
To ensure the fetus reaches macrosomia before the delivery
questions.exp: The listed health-based indication for MTP is to save the pregnant woman's life or to prevent grave physical or mental injury. (Book p427)

questions.q: What fetal indication is listed for MTP?
opts: Rh positivity of the fetus alone, without any other factor
Female sex of the fetus alone, without any other factor
Fetal weight above 3 kg alone, without any other factor
Substantial risk of physical or mental abnormalities in the fetus
questions.exp: The listed fetal indication for MTP is a substantial risk of physical or mental abnormalities in the fetus. (Book p427)

questions.q: Fill up: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2021, termination up to ______ weeks needs the opinion of one registered medical practitioner, and termination between ______ weeks needs two.
questions.exp: Up to 20 weeks one registered medical practitioner suffices; from 20 to 24 weeks two are required for the specified categories of women. (Book p427)

questions.q: Whose consent is required for MTP in a patient aged 18 years or older?
questions.exp: For a patient at least 18 years old, her own consent is required. (Book p427)

questions.q: When is guardian consent required for MTP?
opts: If the patient is under 18 years or mentally unstable
Only if the fetus is female
questions.exp: Guardian consent is required for a minor or mentally unstable patient. (Book p427)

questions.q: How many doctors’ opinions are needed for MTP up to 20 weeks?
questions.exp: Up to 20 weeks, one doctor’s opinion is required. (Book p427)

questions.q: How many doctors’ opinions are needed for MTP from 20–24 weeks?
questions.exp: From 20 to 24 weeks, two doctors’ opinions are required. (Book p427)

questions.q: Are marriage proof and an FIR for rape required records for MTP?
questions.exp: The notes state marriage proof and rape FIR are not required. (Book p427)

questions.q: For at least how long are records of rape maintained according to the notes?
questions.exp: Records of rape are maintained for a minimum of 5 years. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which specialist qualifications are listed for a provider of MTP?
questions.exp: MD, MS, DGO, or DNB in OBG are listed qualifying specialties. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which training pathway qualifies a registered medical practitioner to perform MTP according to the notes?
opts: Attending a single lecture on the MTP Act and its recent amendments
Completing a twenty-four hour online course on termination techniques
No specific clinical training is required of a registered medical practitioner
Assisting at 25 terminations and performing 5, or six months of house job in obstetrics and gynaecology
questions.exp: The Act requires practical training: assisting at 25 procedures and performing 5, or an equivalent period of obstetric training. (Book p427)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about consent under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act is TRUE?
opts: The woman's own consent is required, and for a minor or a woman with mental illness the written consent of a guardian is needed
The husband's signature is mandatory before any termination can be performed
Two registered medical practitioners must examine every woman even when the pregnancy is under 12 weeks
Consent is unnecessary when the woman is unmarried, since the guardian decides
questions.exp: The Act protects the woman's autonomy: her consent governs, with guardian consent only for minors and women with mental illness. (Book p427)

questions.q: What is an advantage of medical abortion compared with surgical abortion?
opts: It is noninvasive and needs no surgical expertise
It is always faster and one step
It has no possibility of failure
questions.exp: Medical abortion is noninvasive and does not require surgical expertise or anesthesia. (Book p427)

questions.q: What is a disadvantage of medical abortion?
opts: It completes in one fast procedure
It may fail and require surgery; it is multistep and longer
questions.exp: Medical abortion can fail requiring surgery and is a longer multistep process. (Book p427)

questions.q: What is an advantage of surgical abortion?
opts: It is a fast, one-time, one-step procedure
questions.exp: Surgical abortion is fast, one-time, and one step. (Book p427)

questions.q: What is a disadvantage of surgical abortion?
opts: It is invasive and has surgical/anesthetic complications
questions.exp: Surgical abortion is invasive and can have surgical and anesthetic complications. (Book p427)

questions.q: Match the method with its role — 1) Mifepristone 2) Misoprostol 3) Manual vacuum aspiration … A) Prostaglandin analogue given 24-48 hours later to expel the products of conception B) Antiprogesterone given first, which primes the cervix and detaches the decidua C) The preferred surgical method up to 12 weeks, suitable for an outpatient setting
questions.exp: Mifepristone sensitises the uterus to prostaglandin, misoprostol expels the pregnancy, and manual vacuum aspiration is the surgical option in the first trimester. (Book p427)
